result:
All questions researched. Here are the answers.

---

**h01** — S3 presign refresh runner — every 12 hours — wired at `server/server.go:162-171`

- Component: `s3presign.Runner` (`server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:16`), whose `CheckAndPresign` (`runner.go:47`) re-signs S3 object URLs whose `LastPresignedTime` is older than 4 days (URLs expire at 5 days) and writes the new `Reference` back via `Store.UpdateAttachment` (`runner.go:116`).
- Schedule: `runnerInterval = time.Hour * 12` (`server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:27`), ticker loop in `Run` (`runner.go:29-41`).
- Wiring: `Server.startBackgroundRunners` — `s3presign.NewRunner(s.Store)` at `server/server.go:162`, one immediate `RunOnce(ctx)` at `server/server.go:163`, then the goroutine `Run(s3Context)` at `server/server.go:169`. `startBackgroundRunners` is called from `Server.Start` (`server/server.go:129`).

**h02** — delivery function: `webhook.Post` — `internal/webhook/webhook.go:120` (HTTP executed at `webhook.go:152`, `safeClient.Do(req)`); protection: dial-time reserved/private-IP blocking

- `safeClient` with `Transport.DialContext = safeDialContext` — `internal/webhook/webhook.go:32-37`; `safeDialContext` resolves the host and rejects any reserved IP — `internal/webhook/webhook.go:59-77`. Because the check happens at dial time it also defeats DNS rebinding.
- Backing predicate `isReservedIP` + CIDR list (loopback, RFC-1918, 169.254/16 IMDS, IPv6 equivalents) — `internal/webhook/validate.go:14-54`; escape hatch `AllowPrivateIPs` — `internal/webhook/validate.go:41`.
- Second, earlier layer: `webhook.ValidateURL` (`internal/webhook/validate.go:62`) at webhook create/update — `server/router/api/v1/user_service_webhooks.go:74,161,182`.

**h03** — abstraction package: `internal/idp` (`internal/idp/idp.go`, defines `IdentityProviderUserInfo`); implementation package: `internal/idp/oauth2` (`internal/idp/oauth2/oauth2.go:20` `IdentityProvider`, constructor at `:26`). OAuth2 is the only concrete protocol implementation that ships.

**h04** — no

- `mysql.NewDB` is defined at `store/db/mysql/mysql.go:20` and the only call site anywhere is the factory `NewDBDriver` at `store/db/db.go:22`.
- Evidence: repo-wide grep for `mysql.NewDB` / `NewDBDriver` yields only `store/db/db.go:22` plus the definition; the two other direct driver constructions in the tree are `sqlite.NewDB` in tests (`store/demo_seed_test.go:24`, `store/deployment_config_test.go:416`) — MySQL has no such direct construction, in tests or production. Test helpers go through the factory (`store/test/store.go:28,50`).

**h05** — explicit Go code (two statements), not a DB-level cascade

- Explicit deletes inside the delete-user transaction: `deleteReactionsByContentIDsTx` (reactions *on* the user's memos, keyed `memos/<uid>`) — `store/db/sqlite/user_delete.go:376-384`, and `deleteReactionsByCreatorTx` (reactions *authored by* the user) — `store/db/sqlite/user_delete.go:396-399`; both invoked from `deleteUserTargetsTx` at `store/db/sqlite/user_delete.go:92,98`. Entry point `(*DB).DeleteUser` — `store/db/sqlite/user_delete.go:29` (mirrored per driver; `store.Driver.DeleteUser` — `store/driver.go:48`, `Store.DeleteUser` — `store/user.go:171`).
- Checked and ruled out a database rule: the `reaction` table has no foreign keys and no `ON DELETE CASCADE` — `store/migration/sqlite/LATEST.sql:92-99`, `store/migration/mysql/0.20/00__reaction.sql:2-8`, `store/migration/postgres/0.20/00__reaction.sql`. No trigger definitions exist for it either.

**h06** — handlers and convergence point

| RPC handler | path | dispatch hop |
|---|---|---|
| `APIV1Service.CreateMemo` | `server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:70` | `DispatchMemoCreatedWebhook` @ `:157` |
| `APIV1Service.UpdateMemo` | `server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:401` | → `dispatchMemoUpdatedSideEffects` → `DispatchMemoUpdatedWebhook` @ `server/router/api/v1/memo_update_helpers.go:67` |
| `APIV1Service.DeleteMemo` | `server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:518` | `DispatchMemoDeletedWebhook` @ `:562` |
| `APIV1Service.CreateMemoComment` | `server/router/api/v1/memo_service_comments.go:20` | `DispatchMemoCommentCreatedWebhook` @ `:119` |

All four funnel through `dispatchMemoRelatedWebhook`/`DispatchMemoCommentCreatedWebhook` → `webhook.PostAsync` (`server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go:43,71`) → the bounded queue `asyncPostQueue` (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:39`, 4 workers at `:42-55`).

Convergence function: **`webhook.Post` — `internal/webhook/webhook.go:120`** (the single place the outbound request is built and executed).

**h07**

```
serveUserAvatar                — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:168   (route GET /file/users/:identifier/avatar registered at :124)
FileServerService.getUserByUsername — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:715
Store.GetUser                  — store/user.go:148   (userCache lookup at :150, cache fill at :167)
Store.ListUsers                — store/user.go:~140 → s.driver.ListUsers
store.Driver.ListUsers (iface) — store/driver.go:47
(*sqlite.DB).ListUsers         — store/db/sqlite/user.go:88   (mysql: store/db/mysql/user.go:84; postgres: store/db/postgres/user.go:87)
```
The image bytes themselves are not a separate table read: `user.AvatarURL` holds a data URI, decoded by `parseDataURI` and MIME-checked against `avatarAllowedTypes` (`fileserver.go:196-203`, allowlist at `:75`) before `c.Blob` at `:209`.

**h08** — two declarers

| declarer | invoked from production? | caller |
|---|---|---|
| `s3presign.Runner` — `server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:43` | yes | `Server.startBackgroundRunners` — `server/server.go:163`; also self-invoked on the ticker in `Run` — `server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:36` |
| `memopayload.Runner` — `server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:27` | no | no callers at all (not even tests); `memopayload.NewRunner` (`runner.go:19`) is never called. Only the package's free function `RebuildMemoPayload` (`runner.go:74`) is used, from `server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:108,447` |

**h09** — 9 declarations total (6 concrete non-test + 1 interface method + 2 test-only); 5 concrete declarers are reached from non-test server code

Declarations:
- `(*Store).Close` — `store/store.go:72`
- `(*cache.Cache).Close` — `store/cache/cache.go:187`
- `(*sqlite.DB).Close` — `store/db/sqlite/sqlite.go:67`
- `(*mysql.DB).Close` — `store/db/mysql/mysql.go:47`
- `(*postgres.DB).Close` — `store/db/postgres/postgres.go:46`
- `(*SSEHub).Close` — `server/router/api/v1/sse_hub.go:99`
- interface: `store.Driver.Close` — `store/driver.go:11`
- test-only: `store/test/filter_helpers_test.go:200`, `:282`

Invoked from non-test server code:
- `(*Store).Close` ← `Server.Shutdown` — `server/server.go:146`
- `(*SSEHub).Close` ← `Server.closeLongLivedConnections` — `server/server.go:206`
- `(*cache.Cache).Close` (×3 caches) ← `Store.Close` — `store/store.go:74-76`
- `(*sqlite.DB).Close` / `(*mysql.DB).Close` / `(*postgres.DB).Close` ← `s.driver.Close()` in `Store.Close` — `store/store.go:78` (which concrete one runs depends on the selected driver; sqlite by default)

The three test-helper `Close` methods and nothing else are unreached from production. (`(*postgres.DB).Close` is reachable only when `--driver postgres`.)

**h10** — `(*filter.Engine).CompileToStatement` — `internal/filter/engine.go:74` — ~38 call sites

Runner-up is `filter.NewEngine` (`internal/filter/engine.go:24`, ~32). Note most of `CompileToStatement`'s fan-in is test code; its 7 non-test callers are `server/router/api/v1/attachment_service.go:413`, `server/router/api/v1/shortcut_service.go:356`, `store/db/{sqlite,mysql,postgres}/memo_relation.go:85/78/87` (+`:98` postgres), and `internal/filter/helpers.go:11`.

**h11** — 1st: `store.User` (7 packages); 2nd: `store.Memo` (6 packages)

- `store.User` — `store/user.go:29` — referenced from `server/auth`, `server/notification`, `server/router/api/v1`, `server/router/api/v1/test`, `server/router/fileserver`, `server/router/frontend`, `server/router/rss` (~30 files).
- `store.Memo` — `store/memo.go` — referenced from `server/notification`, `server/router/api/v1`, `server/router/api/v1/test`, `server/router/frontend`, `server/router/rss`, `server/runner/memopayload` (~21 files).
- Next tier: `store.Attachment` (4 packages), then `store.MemoRelation` / `store.Inbox` / `store.MemoShare` (3 each).

**h12** — concrete method: `(*sqlite.DB).CreateMemo` — `store/db/sqlite/memo.go:16` (the `INSERT INTO memo (...)` built at `:17-40`)

Determination (static, not guessed from naming): the `driver` flag defaults to `"sqlite"` in both viper and the pflag definition — `cmd/memos/main.go:122` and `cmd/memos/main.go:130` — and is copied into `Profile.Driver` at `cmd/memos/main.go:43`. `store/db/db.go:14-27` switches on `profile.Driver`, so the `"sqlite"` arm at `store/db/db.go:20` (`sqlite.NewDB`) supplies the `store.Driver`. `Store.CreateMemo` (`store/memo.go:109`) only validates the UID and delegates to `s.driver.CreateMemo` (`store/memo.go:113`), so the interface method `store.Driver.CreateMemo` (`store/driver.go:29`) binds to the sqlite implementation. The mysql (`store/db/mysql/memo.go:16`) and postgres (`store/db/postgres/memo.go:16`) candidates are unreachable without `--driver mysql|postgres`.

**h13** — impl: the unexported `service` struct — construction: `markdown.NewService` — holders: three components

- Implementation: `service` — `internal/markdown/markdown.go:58` (the only implementation of `markdown.Service`, `internal/markdown/markdown.go:31`; e.g. `ExtractAll` at `:356`, `RenderHTML`, `GenerateSnippet` at `:264`).
- Constructed by `markdown.NewService(opts...)` — `internal/markdown/markdown.go:85`; the single production call site is `server/router/api/v1/v1.go:48` (test helper: `server/router/api/v1/test/test_helper.go:44`). One instance is shared.
- Interface holders: `APIV1Service.MarkdownService` (`server/router/api/v1/v1.go:35`), `RSSService.MarkdownService` (`server/router/rss/rss.go:45`, injected at `server/server.go:85`), and `memopayload.Runner.MarkdownService` (`server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:16`) — plus the free function `RebuildMemoPayload(_, memo, markdownService markdown.Service)` (`server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:74`).

**h14** — computation site: `memopayload.RebuildMemoPayload` — `server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:74`

- It calls `markdownService.ExtractAll` (`runner.go:80`; implementation `internal/markdown/markdown.go:356`) and assigns `memo.Payload.Tags` and `memo.Payload.Property` (`runner.go:85-86`).
- Triggers: `CreateMemo` — `server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:108`; `UpdateMemo` when content changes — `server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:447`; and the (currently uncalled) bulk rebuild `memopayload.Runner.RunOnce` — `server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:52`.
- Extracted: `Tags` (`#tag` nodes) and `MemoPayload_Property` = `HasLink`, `HasTaskList`, `HasCode`, `HasIncompleteTasks`, `Title` (first-H1 heading text) — `proto/gen/store/memo.pb.go:85-95`, populated at `internal/markdown/markdown.go:386-402`. (`ExtractAll` also returns `Mentions`, which is not stored on the payload.)

**h15** — enforcement sites (7 distinct)

```
APIV1Service.checkMemoReadAccess (single-memo reads: GetMemo :356, parent memo :367)  — server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:39
APIV1Service.ListMemos (VisibilityList / creator-or-PUBLIC|PROTECTED filter injection) — server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:218-227
APIV1Service.ListMemoComments (visibility filter for comment listing)                  — server/router/api/v1/memo_service_comments.go:156-161
APIV1Service.CreateMemoComment (PRIVATE parent blocks non-owner comments)              — server/router/api/v1/memo_service_comments.go:41
APIV1Service.ListMemoAttachments (memo visibility gate on attachment listing)          — server/router/api/v1/memo_attachment_service.go:213-222
FileServerService.checkAttachmentPermission (raw file/thumbnail serving)               — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:674-699
SSEClient.canReceive (server-side filtering of pushed memo events)                     — server/router/api/v1/sse_hub.go:134-144
```
Two more surfaces enforce it by restricting the query to PUBLIC rather than by checking a viewer:
```
RSSService.GetExploreRSS / GetUserRSS (VisibilityList = {Public})                       — server/router/rss/rss.go:90, :141
FrontendService.getSitemapXML (VisibilityList = {Public})                               — server/router/frontend/frontend.go:150
```
Plus `canViewerAccessMemo` for notification/inbox delivery — `server/router/api/v1/user_service_notifications.go:302-312`.

**r01** — Premise is wrong: there is no Redis anywhere in this repo (no `redis` import in `go.mod`, no reference in any `.go` file), so there is no Redis connection to configure.

Actual mechanism: a process-local in-memory cache, `store/cache/cache.go` (`Cache` at `:67`, `New` at `:76`). `Store` holds three instances — `instanceSettingCache`, `userCache`, `userSettingCache` — `store/store.go:27-29`, created at `store/store.go:51-53` from one config literal at `store/store.go:39-45`. User entries use the shared `DefaultTTL` of **10 minutes**, with a 5-minute cleanup sweep and a 1000-item cap (`store/store.go:40-42`; identical defaults in `cache.DefaultConfig` — `store/cache/cache.go:57-64`). Users are cached in `Store.GetUser` (`store/user.go:150,167`). Nothing is shared across processes.

**r02** — Premise is wrong: there is no rate-limiting middleware in this codebase — per-user or otherwise — so nothing is registered and there are no limits.

Only two Echo middlewares are registered: `middleware.Recover()` and `newCORSMiddleware(profile)` — `server/server.go:51-52`. The Connect interceptor chain is `MetadataInterceptor` and `LoggingInterceptor` only — `server/router/api/v1/connect_interceptors.go:22,98`. The gRPC-Gateway middleware does authentication/authorization, not throttling — `server/router/api/v1/v1.go:69-85`. The sole occurrence of the phrase in Go source is an aspirational comment about email sending — `internal/email/doc.go:86`.

**r03** — Premise is wrong: there is no nightly database-cleanup job, and no cron scheduler is running.

`internal/scheduler` exists as a standalone cron library (`ParseCronExpression` — `internal/scheduler/parser.go:30`; `Register` — `internal/scheduler/scheduler.go:68`), but it is never instantiated by production code: every `scheduler.New(...)` / `s.Register(...)` call is in `internal/scheduler/integration_test.go` and `example_test.go`. The `"0 9 * * *"` expression you may find is test data (`internal/scheduler/integration_test.go:183`), not a configured job. The only real background work is the S3 presign runner on a 12-hour `time.Ticker`, not cron — `server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:27-41`, started at `server/server.go:169`.

**r04** — Premise is wrong: neither. There is no message broker in this project — no NATS, RabbitMQ, or AMQP dependency or reference anywhere — and therefore no queue declaration.

Actual mechanism: webhook delivery is in-process. `webhook.PostAsync` (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:184`) does a non-blocking send into a buffered Go channel, `asyncPostQueue = make(chan *WebhookRequestPayload, 128)` — `internal/webhook/webhook.go:39`. Four goroutine workers are started in the package `init()` (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:42-55`) and each calls `webhook.Post` (`:120`). Overflow is dropped with a warning, not persisted (`:191-195`), so pending deliveries are lost on restart.

**r05** — Premise is wrong: there is no GraphQL schema, server, or dependency in this repo.

Actual API surface: Protobuf/gRPC definitions under `proto/api/v1`, generated into `proto/gen/api/v1`, exposed over HTTP two ways from `APIV1Service.RegisterGateway` (`server/router/api/v1/v1.go:65`) — a grpc-gateway REST/JSON transcoding layer, and Connect RPC handlers (`server/router/api/v1/connect_handler.go`, `connect_services.go`, generated clients in `proto/gen/api/v1/apiv1connect/`). Alongside that: an SSE stream (`server/router/api/v1/sse_handler.go`), a plain-HTTP file server (`server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:124`), RSS feeds (`server/router/rss/rss.go`), an MCP endpoint (`server/server.go:92-96`), and `/healthz` (`server/server.go:67`).
